verdict.rationale: Better Auth's own API Key plugin lets an app create, manage and verify API keys. Those keys can be bounded with expiration times, usage counts, refills, rate limits and organization ownership. The homepage also claims 'agent delegation' and an MCP OAuth authorization-server plugin. However, the evidence never documents permission or scope restrictions on keys or agent-specific least-privilege grants, so only the bounding half of the story is shown. Missing for 10: documented per-key permission/scope assignment, docs detailing agent delegation or token-exchange scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: The API Key plugin allows you to create and manage API keys for your application. It provides a way to authenticate and authorize API requests by verifying API keys.
Custom expiration times, remaining count, and refill systems
Organization-owned API keys in addition to user-owned keys
Auth for AI agents. MCP auth, token exchange, and agent delegation.
The **MCP** plugin lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) clients.
